Expectation1: Listen actively and provide emotional support when needed.
Situation1: Your friend calls you in the middle of the night, crying, because they just received some devastating family news.
Expectation2: Ensure compliance with safety and regulatory standards
Situation2: A recently updated standard will apply to the upcoming release, and evidence of conformity is required
Story:
My phone buzzed violently on the nightstand, jolting me awake. It was 2:13 a.m. I squinted at the screen—Sam. I answered, and immediately heard sobs. Through broken words, Sam told me about the news: his father had collapsed, and the prognosis was grim. He needed me to listen, to be there, to help him make sense of the chaos. I sat up, heart pounding, trying to offer comfort, to be the friend he needed.

But as I listened, my mind kept drifting to the email I’d read before bed. The new safety standard for our project was now in effect, and the compliance documentation was due by 8 a.m. Without it, the release would be delayed, and the team would face serious consequences. I was the only one who understood the new requirements well enough to pull everything together in time.

Sam’s voice trembled in my ear, desperate for reassurance. At the same time, the weight of my responsibility as an engineer pressed down on me. I felt torn, guilt gnawing at me from both sides, as I tried to be present for my friend while my mind raced with technical checklists and looming deadlines.
